title: Running a compute shader with a texture that was shared with `RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_extension()` crashes the engine when using the D3D12 driver
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.dev2, v4.6.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev2 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (AMD; tested with both 25.10.2 and 26.2.2) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 (12 threads) - 31.90 GiB memory

### Issue description

Running a compute shader on a local rendering device with a texture that was shared from the main rendering device using `RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_extension()` causes a series of errors in the rendering backend, ultimately crashing the engine.
This only occurs when using the D3D12 driver. When using the Vulkan driver, the compute shader executes without any errors and produces the expected result.

The first error is thrown when the compute pipeline is submitted and stems from `RenderingDeviceDriverD3D12::command_buffer_end()` where `cmd_buf_info->cmd_list->Close()` returns `E_INVALIDARG`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the D3D12 driver
2. Create a texture on the main rendering device
3. Share the texture with a local rendering device using `RenderingDevice.texture_create_from_extension()`
4. Use the texture in a compute list on the local rendering device
